To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a sinuous depression with a minimum volume loss of 1.83⋅106m3 and an average subsidence of 0.2 m yr –1 is developing along the eastern Dead Sea, that sinkholes are forming in the subsided zone, that subrosion is an important process behind the development of the sinkholes, and that sinkholes and the sinuous depression are linked to preferential groundwater flows along wadis.
the sinuous depression is a kilometer-scale subsided zone that is partly bound by flexure and by non-tectonics faults.

a kilometer-scale, sinuous, subsided depression, partly bound by flexures and partly by non tectonic faults is developing at Ghor Al Haditha, and is the main cause of the sinkhole hazard in this region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a major geological hazard, but it also contributes to the scientific understanding of the Dead Sea sinkhole hazard and to the development of a hazard mitigation strategy.
the first detailed description and analysis of the subsidence and associated sinkholes on the eastern Dead Seashore, which is a region where sinkhole hazard has been poorly documented.
the first comprehensive description of the subsidence and associated sinkhole hazard in the eastern shore of Dead Sea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
subrosion, rather than dissolution, is the key process behind sinkhole development in the Dead Sea eastern shore.
the sinkhole and subsidence hazards are a consequence of the interaction between the Dead Sea’s rapid drop in water level, the local geology and the regional hydrology.
subrosion, in addition to karst dissolution, is the main process behind the development of the subsided zone and the formation of sinkholes in the Ghor Al-Hadditha area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Dead Sea shore subsidence is the consequence of a complex combination of geological processes, which include tectonics, karstification and subrosion.

the sinuous depression is the result of the interaction between tectonic and non-tectonic processes and that subrosion, in addition to karst dissolution, is a key process behind the subsidence hazard.

the subsidence and subsequent sinkhole hazard is the result of the interplay between the following processes: (1) groundwater extraction, (2) the development of artesian springs, (3) channelized, sediment laden flows, (4) subrosion and (5) the presence of a preferential flow path in the form of the sinuous main depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subrosion and groundwater flow paths play a major role in the subsidence and development of sinkholes in the eastern Dead Sea area.
the subsidence and subsurface erosion processes are closely linked and that their evolution is controlled by the regional groundwater flow.
subrosion is a key physical mechanism behind subsidence, and that sinkhole hazard is linked to the sinuous subsidence depression, which in turn is related to the wadis.
